newsitem.title: QATAR: Philippines seeks Gulf Arab role in its oil sector.
newsitem.headline: Philippines seeks Gulf Arab role in its oil sector.

text.p: Philippines President Fidel Ramos on Sunday urged Gulf Arab states to pump capital into his country's oil industry.

"The deregulation of the oil sector in the Philippines has opened vast opportunities for oil-producing countries and we invite Gulf states to invest in our downstream industries," he told reporters at the start of a two-day visit to Qatar.
"We have big gas deposits in some parts of the country and we need billions of dollars to develop them and set up gas-based industries," he added.

Ramos, visiting Qatar at the invitation of the emir, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani, is expected to sign an economic, commercial and technical cooperation agreement and a labour treaty with Qatar on Monday.

Qatar is home to around 33,000 Filipino workers, but trade between the two countries has been less than one percent of the Philippines' overseas trade. Bilateral trade in the 11 months to November 1996 amounted to $41.62 million, with Manila posting a $38.12 million deficit.
"A joint business council will be set up under the agreement to find ways and means of boosting the trade and a seperate protocol on protection of investments will be signed," Ramos said.
"We are trying to set up a joint bilateral commission with Gulf states to protect the rights of workers and deal with their recurring problem of welfare," he said.
Many Filipino workers in the Gulf have been known to be involved in disputes with their employers over alleged mistreatment.
Ramos is accompanied by a delegation including Filipino Moslem leader Nur Misuari, the governor of the autonomous region of Mindanao. He leaves for Manama on Monday.
